variants.name: faceted
variants.prompt:
Create a polished 3D gameplay art-direction mockup for Facet TD, using the supplied local reference image as a STRICT composition, board geometry, camera and HUD template. This is an edit/style exploration, not a layout redesign.
Reference image: current cave-grey isometric desktop mockup. Output exactly ONE landscape gameplay screenshot, same aspect and framing; no collage, inset, title poster, device frame or new controls.
NON-NEGOTIABLE STRUCTURE: retain the complete 37x37 playable board, original diamond projection and all seven marker positions and labels EXACTLY as in the reference: S at the upper apex region, 1 upper-left wall opening, 2 lower-right wall opening, 3 right-side outer point, 4 upper-right wall opening, 5 lower-left wall opening, E near bottom apex. Never swap 2/3 or 4/5. Retain all four short wall arms and open checkpoint gaps; no added walls, bridges, stairs or terrain inside the playable grid. Preserve the dotted route and three gem locations and selected ruby ring. No enemies or extra towers.
HUD: preserve charcoal-grey top status bar, top-left five gem slots (three filled, two empty), bottom-left Normal ruby selection panel and bottom-right ICON-ONLY toolstrip. Keep grey UI and clean readable sans-serif text, not pixel fonts. Keep interface labels and values as shown. No green UI, no green terrain, no invented buttons. You may omit the small development annotation above the toolstrip. Gem pigments are red ruby, blue sapphire, purple amethyst.
READABILITY: bright matte slate-grey board, restrained dark-grey cave perimeter, soft neutral key light, subtle contact shadows. Low stone walls and compact gems must never obscure cell boundaries or checkpoint numbers. Cave scenery stays OUTSIDE the board and is modest: rock ledges and a few mineral outcrops, not a huge cavern illustration. The board remains the dominant playable area. No bloom, neon floods, reflective floor or depth-of-field blur. This is plausible production browser-game rendering, not cinematic concept painting.
STYLE FOR THIS VARIANT: FACETED LOW-POLY. All cave rock, small wall stones, gem sockets and crystalline gems use deliberately cut angular polygon faces with broad planar shading. Irregular fractured rock edges and triangular rock planes, without a cubic voxel staircase aesthetic. The three gems use clean readable crystal cuts. Quiet material surfaces; no tiny texture noise.
